title: Smashed Chickpea Salad Wrap
summary: A no-cook wrap from pantry staples: canned chickpeas, a creamy dressing, and crunchy vegetables. Teaches two techniques: mashing to a chunky texture and folding a filling evenly.

steps.title: Quick-pickle the onion
steps.instruction: Put the sliced red onion in a small cup with 1 tbsp lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Let it sit while you work.
steps.cue: The onion turns brighter pink and softens. It takes about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Mash the chickpeas
steps.instruction: Put the drained chickpeas in the bowl and press with a masher or fork until most are broken.
steps.cue: Mostly broken and chunky, only a few whole chickpeas left, not a smooth paste.

steps.title: Dress and fold
steps.instruction: Add mayo, mustard, 1 tbsp lemon juice, celery, bell pepper, the drained onion, salt and pepper. Fold from the bottom up until evenly mixed.
steps.cue: Red and green pieces spread through the whole bowl, everything lightly coated, no white streaks of dressing.

steps.title: Fill and roll
steps.instruction: Spoon about half the filling in a line across the lower third of a tortilla. Fold in the sides, then roll away from you.
steps.cue: A spoonful holds its shape. If it slumps or pools, it is too wet to roll.

checkpoints.target: Most chickpeas are broken into coarse, crumbly pieces. Fewer than about 10 whole chickpeas are visible. It is chunky, not smooth like hummus.
Red pepper and celery pieces are spread across the whole bowl, everything is lightly coated, and there are no white streaks or pools of dressing.

reviewedSubstitutions.note: Lettuce leaves make it gluten-free; check bread labels.

adjustmentLabels.mash_side: Focus on the side with more whole chickpeas
adjustmentLabels.fine_as_is: Smoother than the target is still fine to use
adjustmentLabels.fold_from_bottom: Scrape from the bottom and fold up
adjustmentLabels.add_chickpeas_if_wet: If it looks wet, stir in a few more mashed chickpeas
